result.topic_en: Euler proves (λ/λ) = 2cos(λπ/n)(λ/(n−2λ)) for his integral notation (p/q) and combines it with Theorem (23), via x = y^n, to obtain a new theorem linking π/(n tan(λπ/n)) to an integral with a logarithmic factor; for λ = 1 this gives a proportion involving tan(π/n).
result.transcription:
162
$\int\frac{y^{p-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{n-q}}}$
hoc charactere: $\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)$, ac demonstrandum est esse:
$\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-\lambda}\right)=\frac{2\pi\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}{n\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-2\lambda}\right)$.
Iam primum demonstraui, si fuerit $q+r=n$, fore
$\left(\frac{q}{r}\right)=\frac{\pi}{n\sin.\frac{q\pi}{n}}$,
vnde statim sequitur
$\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-\lambda}\right)=\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{\lambda}}}=\frac{\pi}{n\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}$,
ita vt demonstrandum restet esse:
$\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda}\right)=2\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-2\lambda}\right)$.
Verum ibidem ostendi, si fuerit $p+q+r=n$, fore
$\frac{1}{\sin.\frac{r\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)=\frac{1}{\sin.\frac{q\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{p}{r}\right)=\frac{1}{\sin.\frac{p\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{q}{r}\right)$.
Sumamus igitur $p=\lambda$, $q=\lambda$, eritque $r=n-2\lambda$, quo, ob $\sin.\frac{(n-2\lambda)\pi}{n}=\sin.\frac{2\lambda\pi}{n}$, colligimus,
$\frac{1}{\sin.\frac{2\lambda\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda}\right)=\frac{1}{\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-2\lambda}\right)$,
ita vt, ob
$\sin.\frac{2\lambda\pi}{n}=2\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}$, fit reuera
$\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda}\right)=2\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}\left(\frac{\lambda}{n-2\lambda}\right)$.
Multo magis autem abstrusum est Theorema supra (23) erutum,

163
erutum, quod sub iisdem integrationum terminis fit:
$\frac{\pi}{\sin.n\pi}\int x^{n}dx.(1-x)^{n-1}=\int\frac{dx}{x}\int\frac{x^{n-1}dx}{(1-x)^{n}}$ [?]
seu
$\frac{\pi}{2\sin.n\pi}\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{n-1}=\int\frac{dx}{x}\int\frac{x^{n-1}dx}{(1-x)^{n}}$ [?],
quae aequatio vt ad illam formam reducatur, loco $n$ scribamus $\frac{\lambda}{n}$, sitque $x=y^n$; vnde fit
$\frac{\pi}{2n\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{n-\lambda}}}=\int\frac{dy}{y}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{\lambda}}}$.
Modo autem vidimus esse
$\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{n-\lambda}}}=2\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{2\lambda}}}$,
sicque vi huius Theorematis colligimus esse:
$\frac{\pi}{n\tang.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{2\lambda}}}=\int\frac{dy}{y}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{\lambda}}}$,
hincque porro istud Theorema non minus notatu dignum:
$\frac{\pi}{n\tang.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{2\lambda}}}=-\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy\,.\,ly}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{\lambda}}}$,
vnde sumto $\lambda=1$ sequentem proportionem elicimus:
$\frac{\pi}{n}:\tang.\frac{\pi}{n}=\int\frac{dy\,l\frac{1}{y}}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)}}:\int\frac{dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{2}}}$,
